svg.title: The 1588 Spanish Armada: Channel Battles, Calais Fireships & Atlantic Wrecks (May–Oct 1588)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 7 historical GIS atlas map of the 1588 Spanish Armada voyage and wrecks on an unpartitioned British Isles and welded 16th-century European base, showing Spain and Portugal (Lisbon and Corunna), England and Wales, the Kingdom of Scotland, unpartitioned Ireland, Spanish Netherlands (Parma at Dunkirk), and a zoomed Straits of Dover GIS inset of the Calais Roads midnight fireships and Battle of Gravelines.

text.tspan: Gales wreck galleons off Scotland & Ireland; half lost
130 Spanish ships in crescent; nimble English attack upwind

g.text: ZOOM: STRAITS OF DOVER — CALAIS & GRAVELINES (6–8 AUG)
Spain, Portugal & Spanish Netherlands (Philip II & Parma)
Armada Advance (130 Ships: Lisbon & Corunna → Calais)
English Upwind Pursuit & 8 Calais Midnight Fireships
Only ~67 battered Spanish ships limp back to Santander

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 7 ENQUIRY: CROWN, CHURCH OR PARLIAMENT? (1517–1689)
The 1588 Spanish Armada: Channel Battles, Fireships & Atlantic Wrecks
Nimble race-built English ships, long-range culverin guns, and midnight fireships at Calais shattered Spain’s crescent fleet.
Fierce “Protestant Wind” gales wrecked dozens of Spanish galleons off Scotland and Ireland—saving Elizabeth I’s Protestant throne.
